title: Special Needs: Communicate, Adapt, and What the PCP Adds
next: Chapter 48: Acute Interventions for the Chronic Care Patient

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already adapt how you talk to, lift and move patients. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Communicate across hearing, vision, speech and cognitive challenges
  2. Know what Down syndrome, autism, spina bifida and more change on a call
  3. Know what the PCP adds: the IV site, latex, CPAP or BVM, and the DNR

Textbook: Chapter 47, PDF pages 3996–4037
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter forty-seven: patients with special needs. As EMRs, you already know that some patients need a different way of talking, lifting and moving. The standard assessment doesn't change; you adapt it, and you treat the patient, the family and the caregivers as teammates. As a PCP, there's more to think about: where to put an IV when an arm is paralyzed, which supplies might trigger an allergy, and whether a weak patient needs CPAP or a bag-valve mask. Today we'll cover communicating across different challenges, the conditions you'll meet and what they change, and what the PCP adds.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第四十七章：有特殊需要的患者。作为 EMR，你们已经知道有些病人需要换一种方式沟通、抬举和搬运。标准评估不变，只是要按需调整，并把病人、家属和照护者都当成队友。作为 PCP，要考虑的更多：手臂瘫痪时静脉开在哪里、哪些耗材可能引起过敏、一个肌无力的病人需要 CPAP 还是球囊面罩通气。今天讲三件事：面对不同障碍怎样沟通；你会遇到的病况以及它们改变了什么；PCP 多做什么。

slides.title: Ask first: speech and language
slides.body:
Ask: "How would you like to communicate with me?"

  • Dysarthria: weak speech muscles; slurred, slow words
  • Aphasia: language centre damaged; adult tone, focused questions, less noise
  • Stuttering: be patient; don't finish their sentences
  • Total laryngectomy: no voice, neck stoma; writing or a device
  • Used an interpreter? Document it
slides.say: Start every special-needs call with one question: how would you like to communicate with me? Then give the patient time. Dysarthria means the muscles that shape words are weak or poorly coordinated, so speech is slurred or slow. Aphasia means the brain's language centre is damaged, often by a stroke or head injury. Talk to these patients as adults, use focused questions, and cut the background noise. With stuttering, be patient, and never finish their sentences. After a total laryngectomy there's no voice box; the patient breathes through a stoma in the neck and may write or use a device. If you use an interpreter, document it.
slides.sayZh: 每个特殊需要的病人，都先问一句：你希望怎样和我沟通？然后给他时间。构音障碍是发音的肌肉无力或不协调，说话含糊或缓慢。失语是大脑语言中枢受损，常因卒中或颅脑外伤。和这些病人说话要当成年人对待，用聚焦式问题，并减少背景噪音。口吃的人要有耐心，千万别替他把话说完。全喉切除后没有了喉，病人通过颈部造口呼吸，可能靠写字或发声装置交流。用了翻译，要记录下来。

slides.title: Hearing loss and hearing aids
slides.body:
• Conductive (wax, eardrum): often temporary; sensorineural: permanent
  • Face the patient about 50 cm away; one person asks
  • Don't shout: lower your pitch (80% of loss is high-pitched)
  • Better ear, paper and pen, reverse stethoscope
  • Aid whistles? Not sealed or too loud. Two tries, then box it and bring it
Switched on?→New battery→Tubing kinked?→M, not T→Wax in mould?
slides.say: Hearing loss is either conductive, from earwax, a damaged eardrum or infection, and often temporary, or sensorineural, from the inner ear or its nerve, and permanent. Face the patient about fifty centimetres away, and let one person ask the questions. Don't shout. About eighty percent of hearing loss is for high-pitched sounds, so lower your pitch, or let a crew member with a deeper voice talk. Try the better ear, paper and pen, or the reverse stethoscope: earpieces in the patient's ears while you speak softly into the chest piece. A whistling hearing aid isn't sealed or is too loud; after two tries, box it and bring it. If it's silent, check the switch, battery, tubing, the M setting and wax.
slides.sayZh: 听力损失分两类：传导性，来自耵聍、鼓膜损伤或感染，常常是暂时的；感音神经性，来自内耳或听神经，是永久的。面对病人，距离约五十厘米，并且只由一个人提问。别喊。大约百分之八十的听力损失是听不清高音，所以要降低音调，或换声音低沉的队员来说。可以对着听力较好的耳朵说、用纸笔，或者用反向听诊器：把耳件塞进病人耳朵，你对着听头轻声说。助听器啸叫，说明没塞严或音量太大；试两次不行，就放回盒子带上。没声音的话，查开关、电池、导管、是否在 M 档，以及有没有耵聍堵塞。

slides.title: Vision loss
slides.body:
• Clues: glasses, a white cane, a service dog
  • Say who you are; introduce everyone in the room
  • Describe sounds and actions before you move them
  • Guide with a light touch on the elbow; never push
  • Warn of obstacles: "Three steps down"
  • Bring cane, walker, glasses; don't pet the working dog
slides.say: With a visually impaired patient, look for glasses, a white cane or a service dog. Announce yourself when you walk in, and introduce everyone in the room. A busy scene can be frightening when you can't see, so describe what's happening, and always say what you're about to do before you move them. To walk them out, offer a light touch on the elbow, or let them rest a hand on your shoulder, and never push. Warn of obstacles in plain words, like how many steps are coming. Bring the cane, walker and glasses. And a service dog is working, so don't pet it without permission.
slides.sayZh: 面对视障病人，留意眼镜、白手杖或服务犬。进门先报身份，并介绍屋里每个人。看不见的时候，嘈杂的现场会让人害怕，所以要说明正在发生什么，搬动前一定先说你要做什么。扶他走出去时，轻扶他的肘部，或者让他把手搭在你肩上，绝不能推。用简单的话提前提醒障碍，比如前面有几级台阶。带上手杖、助行器和眼镜。服务犬在工作，没有允许别去摸它。

slides.title: Paralysis: devices and the IV arm
slides.body:
• Hemiplegia: one side (stroke, head injury)
  • Paraplegia: lower body; quadriplegia: all four limbs and trunk
  • Sensation may be lost, or heightened: touch can feel like pain
  • Devices: ventilator, trach, Foley, colostomy, feeding tube, halo
  • Trouble swallowing → choking, aspiration: suction ready
  • PCP: IV and drugs on the unaffected side; check the site often
slides.say: Paralysis means the patient can't move part of the body on purpose. Hemiplegia affects one side, often after a stroke. Paraplegia affects the lower body, and quadriplegia all four limbs and the trunk, usually from a neck injury. Paralysis doesn't always mean numbness; for some, a light touch can hurt. Many rely on equipment: a ventilator, a tracheostomy, a urinary catheter, a colostomy, a feeding tube or a halo. Plan every move, get extra hands, and keep suction ready, because trouble swallowing means choking and aspiration. And here's the PCP point: a paralyzed limb has no muscle tone, so start the IV and give drugs on the unaffected side, and check the site often.
slides.sayZh: 瘫痪是指病人无法主动活动身体的某个部位。偏瘫影响一侧身体，常见于卒中后。截瘫影响下半身，四肢瘫影响四肢和躯干，通常是颈部损伤所致。瘫痪不一定麻木，有的人轻轻一碰就会痛。很多人依赖设备：呼吸机、气管切开、导尿管、结肠造口、喂养管或 halo 头环。每次搬动都要计划好，多叫几个人，并备好吸引器，因为吞咽困难意味着容易噎住和误吸。PCP 的重点在这里：瘫痪肢体没有肌张力，所以静脉通路和给药都选健侧，并经常检查穿刺点。

slides.q: A 70-year-old has left-sided paralysis from an old stroke and needs an IV. Which plan is best?
options: Left arm: it moves less, so the line is less likely to be pulled out
Right arm, the unaffected side, and check the site often
Left arm, and rely on the patient to report pain at the site
No IV: a paralyzed patient can't have vascular access
slides.say: Time for a question. A seventy-year-old has left-sided paralysis from an old stroke and needs an IV. Which plan is best? A, the left arm, because it moves less, so the line is less likely to be pulled out. B, the right arm, the unaffected side, and check the site often. C, the left arm, and rely on the patient to report pain at the site. D, no IV, because a paralyzed patient can't have vascular access. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做题。一位七十岁的病人因陈旧性卒中左侧瘫痪，需要开静脉。哪个方案最好？A 左臂，因为它不怎么动，管路不容易被扯掉；B 右臂，也就是健侧，并经常检查穿刺点；C 左臂，靠病人自己报告穿刺点疼；D 不开静脉，瘫痪病人不能建立静脉通路。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The book advises IV access and drugs on the unaffected side, because a paralyzed limb lacks muscle tone. A sounds practical, but the affected arm is the wrong choice. C is dangerous: the patient may not feel an infiltration, which is fluid leaking into the tissue, so you must look for it yourself, especially after giving a drug. D is wrong; paralysis doesn't rule out an IV. And remember, the IV is a PCP skill; in BC, EMRs don't start IVs.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。书里建议静脉通路和给药选健侧，因为瘫痪肢体没有肌张力。A 听起来实用，但患侧是错误的选择。C 很危险：病人可能感觉不到渗漏，也就是液体漏进组织里，所以你必须自己去查，尤其是给药之后。D 错，瘫痪不代表不能开静脉。还要记住，开静脉是 PCP 的技能；在 BC，EMR 没有静脉通路权限。

slides.title: Bariatric patients
slides.body:
• Obese: 20–30% over ideal weight; about 1 in 4 Canadians
  • Ask how best to move them; never lift by one limb
  • Plan crew, equipment weight limits and the exit; call ahead
  • Lying flat can make breathing hard
  • Obesity hypoventilation: low O₂, high CO₂, too many red cells
  • Check equipment pressure points (clot risk)
slides.say: Obesity means being twenty to thirty percent over ideal weight, and it affects about one in four Canadians. Some of these patients have been treated insensitively by health workers before, so put them at ease and protect their dignity. Ask how they move best, and never lift by one arm or leg. Plan the crew, the equipment and its weight limits, and the exit, and call the hospital early. Very large patients may not breathe well lying flat. Some have obesity hypoventilation, or Pickwickian, syndrome: low oxygen, high carbon dioxide and too many red blood cells. And check for pressure points from straps and equipment, which can cause a blood clot.
slides.sayZh: 肥胖是指超出理想体重百分之二十到三十，约四分之一的加拿大人受影响。有些病人以前被医护人员不体贴地对待过，所以要让他们放松，维护他们的尊严。问他们怎样移动最好，绝不能只拽一条胳膊或一条腿抬。规划好人手、设备及其承重上限和出口，并尽早通知医院。体型很大的病人平躺可能呼吸困难。有些人有肥胖低通气综合征，也叫匹克威克综合征：低氧、高二氧化碳、红细胞过多。还要检查绑带和设备造成的压迫点，它们可能导致血栓。

slides.title: Down syndrome
slides.body:
• Extra chromosome 21: intellectual disability, mild to severe
  • Big tongue, small mouth and nose → hard mask seal and intubation
  • Blocked airway: a jaw thrust often fixes it; unconscious → jaw thrust or NPA
  • Up to 40% have congenital heart disease
  • Seizures common, usually tonic-clonic: manage as usual
  • Thyroid, hearing and vision problems are common
slides.say: Down syndrome, or trisomy twenty-one, comes from an extra chromosome twenty-one and brings an intellectual disability from mild to severe. For you, the airway matters most. A large tongue, a small mouth and nose, and misaligned teeth make a mask seal and intubation hard. If the airway is blocked, a simple jaw thrust may be all you need; in an unconscious patient, use a jaw thrust or a nasopharyngeal airway. Up to forty percent have congenital heart disease, such as holes between the heart chambers, which affects your fluids. Seizures are common, usually tonic-clonic; manage them as usual. Thyroid, hearing and vision problems are common too.
slides.sayZh: 唐氏综合征，也叫 21-三体，是多了一条 21 号染色体，带来轻到重度不等的智力障碍。对你来说，气道最要紧：舌头大、口鼻腔小、咬合不正，使面罩密封和插管都很难。气道梗阻时，简单的推颌法可能就够了；昏迷病人用推颌法或鼻咽通气道。多达百分之四十有先天性心脏病，比如心腔之间的间隔缺损，这会影响你的补液。癫痫常见，多为强直-阵挛发作，照常处理。甲状腺、听力和视力问题也很常见。

slides.title: Autism and developmental disability
slides.body:
• Many are nonverbal, always or under stress
  • Noise and crowds can trigger distress or aggression: cut the stimulation
  • Explain first, then touch distal to proximal (hand before chest)
  • Ask the same question in different ways; check for consistency
  • Pain response may not match the injury
  • One person first; let them see and touch the BP cuff; involve caregivers
slides.say: Autism spectrum disorder affects social interaction, communication and behaviour, and many people with autism don't speak, either always or when stressed. Noise, crowds and commotion can trigger distress or even aggression, so cut the stimulation. Explain before you touch, and work from distal to proximal: the hand before the chest. Ask the same question a few ways to see if the answers match. Read pain carefully; some barely react to a serious injury, while a light touch feels terrible. For any developmental disability, let one crew member build trust first, introduce the others slowly, and let the patient see and touch the blood pressure cuff. Caregivers are your best guides.
slides.sayZh: 自闭症谱系障碍影响社交、沟通和行为，很多自闭症患者不说话，有的终身如此，有的在紧张时才这样。噪音、人多和混乱可能引发痛苦甚至攻击行为，所以要减少刺激。先解释再触碰，从远端到近端：先碰手再碰胸。同一个问题换几种问法，看回答是否一致。疼痛要小心判断：有的人重伤也几乎没反应，轻轻一碰却很难受。面对任何发育障碍，先由一名队员建立信任，再慢慢介绍其他人，让病人先看看、摸摸血压袖带。照护者是你最好的向导。

slides.title: Conditions you'll meet
slides.body:
ConditionOn a call, watch for
Cerebral palsydon't assume intellectual disability; seizures (25%); never force limbs
Spina bifidalatex allergy; brain shunt; may not feel injuries
Multiple sclerosisfalls; numb areas hide injuries; rely on history
Muscular dystrophyweak breathing; heart involved in up to 95%
Myasthenia gravisweakness with activity; crisis = respiratory failure
Cystic fibrosisthick mucus, infection; electrolyte loss → arrhythmias
slides.say: Here are the long-term conditions you'll meet most. In cerebral palsy, about three quarters have some intellectual disability, but never assume it; about a quarter have seizures; and never force stiff limbs into position. Spina bifida brings lower-body paralysis, bladder problems, a latex allergy, and often a shunt draining fluid from the brain; these patients may not feel injuries. Multiple sclerosis causes numbness, weakness and falls, so your history matters more than your exam. Muscular dystrophy weakens breathing, and the heart is involved in up to ninety-five percent. In myasthenia gravis, weakness worsens with activity, and a crisis means respiratory failure. Cystic fibrosis brings thick mucus, infections, and electrolyte problems that can cause arrhythmias.
slides.sayZh: 这些是你最常遇到的长期病况。脑瘫病人约四分之三有一定智力障碍，但千万别想当然；约四分之一有癫痫；僵硬的肢体绝不能硬掰。脊柱裂带来下半身瘫痪、膀胱问题、乳胶过敏，常常还有把脑内液体引流出去的分流管；这些病人可能感觉不到受伤。多发性硬化引起麻木、无力和跌倒，所以病史比体检更重要。肌营养不良会削弱呼吸，多达百分之九十五有心脏受累。重症肌无力的无力在活动后加重，危象就是呼吸衰竭。囊性纤维化带来黏稠的痰、反复感染，以及可引起心律失常的电解质紊乱。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: breathing support
slides.body:
BC Oxygen Administration, CPAP and PEEP guidelines

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Position; oxygen to keep SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Suction ready (weak swallow, thick mucus)
  • Assist ventilation with a BVM if breathing fails
  • Salbutamol for asthma/COPD bronchospasm

PCP adds

  • CPAP: age ≥ 13, awake, follows commands
  • …with RR > 24, SpO₂ < 94% on O₂, accessory muscle use
  • No CPAP: trach, poor mask fit, SBP < 90
  • …or can't follow commands, or hypoventilating
  • PEEP valve on the BVM: start 5 cmH₂O, max 10
slides.say: Breathing trouble is where your PCP tools matter most. The left column is shared by every licence level: position the patient, give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four or higher, have suction ready, assist with a bag-valve mask if breathing fails, and give salbutamol for bronchospasm in asthma or COPD. The right column is new for you. CPAP needs a patient thirteen or older who is awake and follows commands, with a breathing rate over twenty-four, a saturation under ninety-four on oxygen, and accessory muscle use. Many special-needs patients hit BC's contraindications: a tracheostomy, a mask that won't fit, not following commands, or slow, shallow breathing. If breathing is failing, use the bag-valve mask, and as a PCP you can add a PEEP valve, starting at five.
slides.sayZh: 呼吸出问题时，PCP 的工具最能派上用场。左栏是所有执照级别共有的：摆体位，给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上，备好吸引器，呼吸衰竭时用球囊面罩辅助通气，哮喘或 COPD 引起支气管痉挛时给沙丁胺醇。右栏是你新增的：CPAP 要求病人十三岁或以上、清醒并能听从指令，呼吸超过二十四、吸氧下血氧低于九十四、有辅助呼吸肌参与。很多特殊需要的病人会碰上 BC 的禁忌症：气管切开、面罩戴不合适、无法听从指令，或者呼吸慢而浅。呼吸衰竭时就用球囊面罩通气，作为 PCP 你还可以加 PEEP 阀，从五开始。

slides.q: A 35-year-old woman with myasthenia gravis has had a chest infection for 3 days. Now she can barely swallow, her breathing is slow and shallow, SpO₂ 88% on oxygen, and she's getting drowsy. As the PCP, what's your best breathing support?
options: CPAP at 5 cmH₂O, because her SpO₂ is low on oxygen
Assist ventilations with a BVM and consider a PEEP valve
Nasal cannula at 2 L/min, and watch her closely
A salbutamol nebulizer, then reassess in 15 minutes
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. A thirty-five-year-old woman with myasthenia gravis has had a chest infection for three days. Now she can barely swallow, her breathing is slow and shallow, her saturation is eighty-eight percent on oxygen, and she's getting drowsy. As the PCP, what's your best breathing support? A, CPAP at five centimetres of water, because her saturation is low on oxygen. B, assist her ventilations with a bag-valve mask, and consider a PEEP valve. C, a nasal cannula at two litres a minute, and watch her closely. D, a salbutamol nebulizer, then reassess in fifteen minutes. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位三十五岁、有重症肌无力的女士胸部感染三天了。现在她几乎咽不下东西，呼吸慢而浅，吸氧下血氧百分之八十八，人越来越嗜睡。作为 PCP，最好的呼吸支持是什么？A 上 CPAP，五厘米水柱，因为她吸氧下血氧还是低；B 用球囊面罩辅助通气，并考虑加 PEEP 阀；C 鼻导管每分钟两升，密切观察；D 先雾化沙丁胺醇，十五分钟后复评。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Infection can trigger a myasthenic crisis, in which the breathing muscles fail. Slow, shallow breathing with a falling level of consciousness is imminent respiratory failure, and BC says these patients are not CPAP candidates; they need bag-valve-mask ventilation and may benefit from PEEP. So A is wrong. C gives far too little support. D treats bronchospasm, but her problem is weak muscles, not narrow airways.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。感染可诱发肌无力危象，呼吸肌会衰竭。呼吸慢而浅、意识水平下降，就是即将发生的呼吸衰竭，BC 规定这类病人不适合 CPAP，需要球囊面罩通气，并可能受益于 PEEP，所以 A 错。C 支持力度远远不够。D 是治疗支气管痉挛的，而她的问题是肌肉无力，不是气道狭窄。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• IV on the unaffected side; check often: they may not feel infiltration
  • Spina bifida: latex-free gloves, tourniquet and IV supplies
  • Down syndrome with heart failure: fluid only if needed; recheck lungs
  • Cystic fibrosis: electrolyte problems can cause arrhythmias
  • Functional Enquiry: get the baseline from caregivers
slides.say: Now the new things to watch for as a PCP. First, IV sites. Patients with paralysis or spina bifida may not feel fluid leaking into the tissue, so use the unaffected side and look at the site often, especially after a drug. Second, many people with spina bifida are allergic to latex, so make sure your gloves, tourniquet and IV supplies are latex-free; a reaction could become anaphylaxis. Third, in Down syndrome with heart failure, give fluid only if it's really needed, and recheck the lungs. Fourth, in cystic fibrosis, watch for arrhythmias. And fifth, do your Functional Enquiry with the caregiver's help, to learn what's normal for this patient.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲作为 PCP 要新注意的事。第一，静脉穿刺部位：瘫痪或脊柱裂的病人可能感觉不到液体渗进组织，所以选健侧，并经常查看穿刺点，尤其是给药之后。第二，很多脊柱裂患者对乳胶过敏，要确认手套、止血带和静脉耗材都不含乳胶，过敏反应可能发展成过敏性休克。第三，唐氏综合征合并心衰时，只在真正需要时才补液，并复查肺部。第四，囊性纤维化要留意心律失常。第五，借助照护者做系统问诊，了解这位病人平时的正常状态。

slides.title: End of life: DNR doesn't mean no care
slides.body:
• BC: a verifiable DNR or No CPR order is the contraindication to CPR
  • Comfort care continues: oxygen, salbutamol, positioning
  • Doubt about the order or wishes → start CPR, contact medical direction
  • Family insists on CPR despite a DNR: confirm they know of it, then start
  • Keep the DNR with the patient

The book's comfort list includes narcotics; opioids are not on the BC licensing exam (BCEHS P03: a PCP may give SC morphine or hydromorphone after CliniCall).
slides.say: Some calls involve patients at the end of life. In BC, a verifiable DNR or No CPR order is the contraindication to CPR. But a DNR is not an order to stop caring: give oxygen, salbutamol for breathlessness, and a comfortable position. If you doubt the order is valid, or you're unsure what the patient wants, the book says to start resuscitation and contact medical direction. If the family wants CPR despite a DNR, make sure they know it exists; if they still insist, start. And note: the book's comfort list includes narcotics, but opioids aren't on the BC licensing exam; in BCEHS, a PCP may give a palliative patient morphine or hydromorphone under the skin, after a CliniCall consult.
slides.sayZh: 有些出诊面对的是临终病人。在 BC，可核实的 DNR 或「不做 CPR」医嘱是 CPR 的禁忌症。但 DNR 不是停止照护的命令：照样给氧、用沙丁胺醇缓解气促、摆舒适体位。如果你怀疑医嘱是否有效，或者不确定病人的意愿，书里说要先开始复苏，同时联系医疗指导。如果家属不顾 DNR 要求做 CPR，先确保他们知道有这份医嘱；仍坚持的话，就开始复苏。还要注意：书里的舒适措施包括麻醉性镇痛药，但阿片类不在 BC 执照考试范围内；在 BCEHS，PCP 咨询 CliniCall 后，可以给姑息病人皮下注射吗啡或氢吗啡酮。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Ask how they communicate; get the baseline from caregivers
  2. IV on the unaffected side; latex-free for spina bifida
  3. Weak, shallow breathing: BVM ± PEEP, not CPAP; a DNR ≠ no care

Next: Chapter 48, Acute Interventions for the Chronic Care Patient
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: ask every patient how they'd like to communicate, and learn their baseline from family and caregivers; they're part of your team. Two: adapt your PCP tools. Put the IV on the unaffected side and check it often, and use latex-free equipment for spina bifida. Three: when breathing is weak and shallow, or the patient can't follow commands, it's the bag-valve mask, with a PEEP valve if needed, not CPAP. And a DNR never means no care. Next, Chapter forty-eight: acute interventions for the chronic care patient. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三件事。一，问每位病人希望怎样沟通，并向家属和照护者了解他的基线，他们是你团队的一部分。二，调整你的 PCP 工具：静脉开在健侧并经常检查；脊柱裂病人用不含乳胶的器材。三，呼吸弱而浅，或病人无法听从指令时，用球囊面罩通气，必要时加 PEEP 阀，而不是 CPAP。DNR 也绝不等于不管。下一章，第四十八章：慢性护理病人的急性处置。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
